newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 11.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 11.7 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 11.7 percent of its average daily volume of 430.3 million shares, or 50.2 million shares, for the week of September 23-27.
Program trading accounted for an average of 19.5 percent of average daily volume of 436.7 million shares for the week of September 16-20.
Of the average 50.2 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 26.7 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 23.5 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 64.9 million shares a day during the week of September 23-27.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, Nomura Securities conducted most of its program activity for its own account. Morgan Stanley, First Options, Interactive Brokers, and Salomon Brothers executed all or most of their program activity for customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 57.5 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 32.1 percent of program volume from September 23-27.

Between September 23-27, 25.1 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 12.8 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
